claims.claim: The paper reports that tokens with phoneme alignment or simple language-model structure are useful downstream and improve the tested zero-shot and resynthesis proxies.
claims.limitations: The tokenizers, languages, proxy tasks, and resynthesis setup bound the result; token usefulness is not the same as complete spoken meaning.

claims.claim: The paper reports 2.8%/7.1% biased WER with 2,000 words, only 0.3/2.9% absolute degradation at 200,000 entries, 99.99% pruning, and 20 ms query latency on the tested split.
claims.limitations: The reported latency, languages, bias lists, and ASR systems define the boundary; rare names outside the retrieval distribution and interactive user correction remain open.

claims.claim: The challenge reports DER 8.09%, CER 9.48%, and cpCER 11.56% for its top systems, with the largest gain in the joint task.
claims.limitations: Challenge data, camera placement, meeting types, language, and leaderboard protocols define the claim; deployment in unseen rooms or privacy-constrained camera settings remains open.

claims.claim: On 600 Chinese adolescents, the paper reports test accuracy .63, recall .74, and F1 about .67.
claims.limitations: This is a screening model on one challenge dataset, not a diagnosis or safety-tested intervention; age, language, labels, privacy, calibration, and external validation constrain the claim.

claims.claim: The paper reports ROC-AUC .90 and F1 .60, and says 8% labeled data reaches 96% of the full supervised model's performance.
claims.limitations: The labels, videoconference setting, participant population, and definition of negative experience bound the result; detection is not a causal explanation of why a conversation deteriorated.

claims.claim: The study reports a combined-stimulation advantage across all three masker languages and language-specific differences in release from masking.
claims.limitations: Normal-hearing listeners, vocoder simulations, Mandarin targets, and the selected masker languages limit direct claims about real CI users and everyday rooms.

claims.claim: The paper reports up to 5.6% recall@10 improvement for retrieval and 3.2% for classification.
claims.limitations: The video domains, caption generator, CLAP filter, and downstream tasks define the result; spoken conversation and human annotation quality outside those videos remain open.

claims.claim: The paper reports WER 10.06% and 11.8% on the two test subsets, with Parakeet slightly ahead of ContextNet.
claims.limitations: Challenge data, speaker impairment profiles, transcripts, and WER define the boundary; fairness across disorders, user control, and clinical usefulness remain unestablished.
